function: Model aggregation over the air (AirComp) for hierarchical personalized FL; receive beamforming at cloud and edge servers (SCA, not learned) minimizes the aggregation MSE (pp. 4-10).
system: Cloud and two edge servers with K=20 receive antennas each; 10 single-antenna devices per edge server; Rician block fading; no RIS; band not stated (pp. 4-5, 10).
method: Two-layer fully connected network trained by hierarchical personalized federated learning with AirComp aggregation; receive beamformers designed by SCA and Lagrangian duality (non-learned) (pp. 3-4, 10).
data_channel: MNIST and FMNIST with 2 labels per device; simulated 3D layout, path-loss exponent 3, Rician fading with kappa 3; no standard channel model or measurements (p. 10).
test_conditions: Same simulated setting for training and testing (T=200 rounds, R=10, K=20 antennas); only lambda, beta, R are varied, with learning curves per setting; no unseen channel or deployment (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Cloud-side beamforming: SDR and optimal BnB; edge-side: Error-free and IgnInter; FL frameworks: FedAvg, FedProx, pFedMe, HierFedAvg, run with the proposed beamformers (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Test accuracy versus communication rounds of the global and personalized models on MNIST and FMNIST; analysis uses time-averaged aggregation MSE and a convergence bound (pp. 7, 11-12).
complexity: Orders given: cloud beamformer O(N^6) SDR initialization then O(I(N^3)) SCA; edge beamformer O((M+K^2)^3.5) initialization and O(I((N-1)MK^3)) SCA (pp. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 10: "The small-scale fading is modeled as Rician fading with racian factor". Not met: the channel is a custom simulator with path loss exponent 3 and Rician fading, with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "we compare the learning performance of the proposed AirComp-assisted HPFL under different hyperparameters". Not met: only lambda, beta and R are varied; the channel model, K=20 antennas (p. 10), devices per edge server, and datasets stay fixed.
q3_support: p. 10: "the SDR [45] algorithm is used as the baseline". p. 10: "compared to the following baseline FL algorithms, i.e., FedAvg [47], FedProx [33], pFedMe [31], and HierFedAvg [6]". p. 11: "achieves a higher test accuracy compared to FedAvg, FedProx, and HierFedAvg".
q4_support: p. 9: "the computation complexity of solving problem P4 through Algorithm 3 is O(I(N 3 ))". p. 10: "solving P6 through SCA-based algorithm has a complexity of" O(I((N - 1)M K^3)) for the edge beamformer.
q5_support: p. 10: "We consider both the MNIST and FMNIST datasets, where each device is designed to encompass only 2 types of labels to reflect data heterogeneity." Not met: these datasets are for the learning task only, the channels are simulated, and no code link is given.
notes: Included as area 7: the learned element is the FL model trained over AirComp, and the paper solves the over-the-air aggregation (beamforming at edge and cloud, pp. 5-10). The beamformers are optimized by SCA, not learned, which is allowed under the FL rule of the instructions. q3 is borderline and the reviewer should confirm: the FL baselines (p. 10) run with the proposed beamformer, so they differ in the learning rule, and SDR and BnB (Fig. 2, p. 11) are the non-learned comparisons; no earlier published over-the-air aggregation design is compared. q4 counts the complexity of the transceiver design (pp. 9-10). Figures on pp. 11-12 were checked as page images.
